name: anchor-seo-mcp

tools.name: list_properties
tools.description: List all active GSC properties with their account, latest snapshot date, last job status, and whether SF auto-crawl is enabled.

tools.name: list_crawl_configs
tools.description: List available Screaming Frog crawl configs (name, description, whether org-default). Use to pick a conservative config to assign to a property.

tools.name: get_property_crawl_config
tools.description: Show which Screaming Frog crawl config a property uses (default + auto) and whether the hosted fleet auto-crawls it. For the local-crawl recipe: pass write_to and the config file the fleet runs for this property is written there (the .seospiderconfig, nothing passes through the conversation), ready for Screaming Frog's --config so the local crawl fetches the way the fleet does. With no config assigned the fleet runs Screaming Frog defaults; the recipe lists the settings that matter.

write_to.description: Absolute path to write the .seospiderconfig to (created or overwritten)

tools.name: upload_gsc_capture
tools.description: Register a GSC Page Indexing snapshot captured from a signed-in browser (the Local-tier path: no credential ever reaches the platform). Give the bundle ONE of three ways: bundle_path = the file the browser tool saved the capture result to (the usual case on the in-app browser pane; the server reads it, nothing is retyped), dir = a folder of SUMMARY.zip, INDEXED.zip, <item_key>.zip, or files = the base64 ZIPs inline (SUMMARY, INDEXED, one per not-indexed reason keyed by its drill-down item_key) for small captures. Use the gsc-capture recipe, which fetches the exports from the page in seconds. The platform stores them exactly like a scraper run and the importer processes them within minutes.

bundle_path.description: Absolute path of the saved capture result (the tool-result file, or a JSON file holding { files })

dir.description: Absolute path of a folder holding SUMMARY.zip, INDEXED.zip, <item_key>.zip

files.description: Base64 ZIPs keyed SUMMARY, INDEXED, or a drill-down item_key (e.g. CAMYFyAC); for small captures only

snapshot.description: Snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD (default: last date in the summary Chart.csv)

segment.description: Segment name as GSC shows it (default "All known pages")

segment_param.description: GSC pages= value for the segment: ALL_URLS (default), ALL_SUBMITTED_URLS, ALL_NON_SUBMITTED_URLS

tools.name: upload_sf_crawl
tools.description: Send a Screaming Frog crawl run on THIS machine to the platform (the Local-tier crawl path). Pass the folder holding the exports — issues_overview_report.csv (Issues Overview report, required), crawl_overview.csv, internal_html.csv or internal_html.ndjson (Internal:HTML tab), and the Issues:All bulk-export CSVs — as produced by the anchor-seo-local-crawl skill. The files are read from disk by this server and never pass through the conversation. The platform stores them exactly like a fleet crawl; the job shows as complete in get_sf_crawls within a few minutes, then get_audit_report can use it.

dir.description: Absolute path of the export folder on this machine (subfolders one level down are included)

snapshot.description: GSC snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD this crawl belongs to (default: the property's latest snapshot)

gsc_category.description: For a per-issue crawl: the GSC reason whose URLs were crawled, exactly as GSC names it (e.g. "Crawled - currently not indexed")

crawl_name.description: Screaming Frog crawl name, for provenance

tools.name: publish_report
tools.description: Publish a report into Anchor, where the organisation reads it at the returned URL, reviews it and comments inline; the comments come back through get_report_comments. Use it when the steering's deliverable_format is `anchor` (the audit and monitor recipes do), or when the person asks for a report they can share with colleagues who do not use Claude. One slug per report: republishing the same slug appends a new version (nothing is overwritten) and tells you how many comments on the previous version are still open. body is markdown (default) or a self-contained HTML page; body_path reads the file from THIS machine instead (both modes), so a long report never passes through the conversation: write it to a file first, then publish from the path. alt_body / alt_body_path attach the same report in the other format (an HTML page as the main view with a markdown alternate readers can switch to or download). finding_refs lists the audit finding ids the report cites (from get_audit_report), so the page can deep-link to the drill-downs. If the result says needs_confirmation, the organisation's steering wants the person's go for this kind (or for a report with no property): ask them, and only if they agree call again with confirm true; it is recorded on the version. Refused when the organisation turned report publishing off in its steering; an archived slug needs restore true.

slug.description: Stable handle, lowercase letters, digits and dashes: "audible-audit-2026-10-22". Reuse it to publish a new version.

title.description: The report title as the reader sees it

kind.description: audit, monitor, crawl, migration or custom

body.description: The report body: markdown, or a self-contained HTML page (body_format html). Required unless body_path is given.

body_path.description: Absolute path of a .md or .html file on this machine to publish instead of passing body (works in both modes; the format is taken from the extension unless body_format is given)

body_format.description: Default markdown; html for a self-contained page (scripts are stripped by the viewer)

alt_body.description: The same report in the other format (markdown beside an HTML body, or HTML beside markdown); shown as a read-only toggle and download on the report page

alt_body_path.description: Absolute path of the alternate on this machine, instead of alt_body

alt_body_format.description: Format of the alternate; default: the format the body is not

property.description: Domain or property identifier the report is about

snapshot.description: The snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD the report is based on

finding_refs.description: Audit finding ids the report cites (the `id` field of get_audit_report findings), optionally with a label

status.description: draft (default for a new report), in_review, or final; omitted on a republish keeps the current status

confirm.description: true only after the person agreed to a publish the previous call answered with needs_confirmation

restore.description: true to republish a slug that was archived (brings it back with its history)

tools.name: get_gsc_export
tools.description: Fetch a raw GSC export verbatim — the actual CSVs Google produced (≤1,000-row sample per category; see get_data_dictionary). Returns the CSV text, capped at 200KB. Pass category (from list_raw_exports) to select one export. With write_urls_to, the URL column is written one-per-line to that local file (a Screaming Frog list-mode input) and only the count comes back — use this to crawl a GSC category locally without the URLs passing through the conversation.

snapshot.description: GSC snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to latest)

write_urls_to.description: Local file path to write the URL list to (one URL per line); requires category

tools.name: get_pipeline_status
tools.description: Health overview across all active properties: latest snapshot date, account, last GSC job status, SF auto-crawl flag. Use to spot stale properties.

tools.name: list_audit_ready
tools.description: One-call poll for the snapshot-ready trigger: per active property, the latest scraped GSC snapshot and whether its crawl wave is terminal (audit_ready=true ⇒ get_audit_report is complete for that snapshot). Properties that do not auto-queue crawls (crawls_expected=false) are ready on the GSC snapshot alone; their audit_ready_reason is no_crawl until a crawl (the local-crawl recipe) has been uploaded for them, and the audit then has coverage 0. Check snapshot_scrape_status — complete_with_errors means the scrape was partial. Pass since (YYYY-MM-DD) to only see snapshots newer than the last one you processed.

since.description: Only properties whose latest snapshot is after this date

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: List available GSC snapshot dates for a property (most recent first), with report and sampled-URL counts.

tools.name: get_property_overview
tools.description: Indexed / not-indexed / total URL counts per segment for a property at a snapshot (defaults to latest). Counts are true GSC totals (chart_url_count), not the 1k sample.

snapshot.description: GSC snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to latest)

tools.name: get_issue_breakdown
tools.description: Per-category indexing issue counts (critical + non-critical) for a property at a snapshot (defaults to latest).

snapshot.description: GSC snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to latest)

tools.name: get_sf_crawls
tools.description: Screaming Frog crawl jobs for a property, newest first (status, snapshot, GSC category, URL counts, whether the platform queued it). Default 50; the result carries total_count and truncated — pass snapshot to see every job of one wave, or raise limit (max 500).

snapshot.description: Only jobs for this snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: get_audit_report
tools.description: The canonical audit report for a property snapshot: trust status (metric invariants), crawl coverage, and ranked findings. Each finding has severity, an explainable score (traffic-weighted: last-28d GSC clicks over its affected URLs), evidence, trend vs the compare snapshot, opportunity.estimated_traffic, and a machine-readable recommended_action (pass its params to get_finding_urls, or act on action_type="recrawl" with recrawl_issues). Carries a validation_candidates section (reasons whose URLs the crawl shows fixed and live — see get_validation_candidates). Defaults to the latest crawl snapshot compared against the previous one. Shaped for tool budgets: top max_findings (default 15) without per-finding explanation text — findings_shaping reports what was trimmed.

snapshot.description: Crawl snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to latest; see list_audit_snapshots)

compare.description: Compare snapshot YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to the previous one)

tools.name: list_audit_snapshots
tools.description: Crawl snapshot dates available for get_audit_report (most recent first). These are SF-crawl snapshots, distinct from raw GSC report dates (list_snapshots).

tools.name: get_finding_urls
tools.description: Drill into an ISSUE finding from get_audit_report: the affected URLs. Pass the finding's recommended_action.params verbatim (issue_type_id, page_types, snapshot_date). For coverage findings use get_uncrawled_urls instead.

page_types.description: The finding's params.page_types (filters to that URL group)

page_types_mode.description: "all" (default) = URLs matching the full page-type combination (reproduces the finding population); "any" = union

tools.name: get_uncrawled_urls
tools.description: Drill into a COVERAGE finding: GSC-indexed pages on the primary host that the crawl missed (the coverage_gap_pages / coverage_regression population).

tools.name: add_property
tools.description: Register a Search Console property for this organisation so Anchor can hold data for it. Give the property exactly as Search Console names it: `sc-domain:example.com` for a domain property, or the full URL prefix with its trailing slash (`https://www.example.com/`) for a URL-prefix property; a bare host is treated as a domain property. Default mode `local` needs no scraper identity: the data comes from the person's own browser (gsc-capture recipe) and their own Screaming Frog (local-crawl recipe). Mode `hosted` attaches it to the organisation's scraper account instead. A domain another organisation already monitors is refused (one organisation per domain). Idempotent for a property the organisation already has.

property.description: sc-domain:example.com, https://www.example.com/, or a bare host

mode.description: local (default): browser captures + local crawls; hosted: the organisation's scraper account

tools.name: archive_property
tools.description: Remove a property this organisation registered: the usual fix when the registered name turns out not to be a Search Console property (the capture landed on Search Console's property picker instead of the Page indexing report), or a site is no longer monitored. Soft: the property is archived, its snapshots and crawls are kept, pending jobs are cancelled, and the name is free to register again; registering the same property again brings its history back. Only the organisation that registered it can remove it. Ask the person before calling this and tell them what will be removed.

property.description: The property as registered (sc-domain:example.com or https://www.example.com/), or a unique part of it

tools.name: get_briefing
tools.description: START HERE, every session: the standing instructions for working with Anchor (how to use the data, the recipes this server publishes as prompts, the rules), the organisation's steering, and whether this machine's anchor-seo-mcp is behind the published version. Served by the platform, so it is always current. If client.update_available is true, tell the person once what update_note says.

tools.name: get_steering
tools.description: The organisation's standing instructions for you: who is reading (role, team), how they want things written, their priorities in order, what to leave alone, and who receives reports. Call it first in every session and follow it — it outranks the generic reporting style in the skills. If is_default is true nothing has been set: offer to capture it in conversation and save it with set_steering.

tools.name: set_steering
tools.description: Save or update the organisation's steering. Pass only the fields to change; omitted fields keep their value. Use it when the person tells you how they want to be worked with ("we're an in-house team of two, keep it terse, ignore the /blog section, send the weekly digest to…"). Lists replace the stored list. Recorded with who changed it.

role.description: Who is reading and their context, e.g. "in-house SEO lead at a DTC retailer, team of two"

tone.description: How to write, e.g. "terse, numbers first, no jargon, UK spelling"

priorities.description: What matters most, in order (replaces the list)

ignore_rules.description: Sections, hosts, issue types or actions to leave alone (replaces the list)

incident_click_threshold.description: Clicks/28d on a new or worsening Google-actionable finding that make it an incident (default 50)

auto_inspect_incidents.description: Let get_incidents spend URL Inspection quota on top incident URLs automatically (default true)

report_recipients.description: Email addresses that receive digests (replaces the list)

deliverable_format.description: How to deliver reports and dashboards: markdown in chat (default), artifact (a Claude Artifact page whenever the Artifact tool is available), or anchor (published into Anchor with publish_report, where the organisation reviews and comments)

report_publishing_enabled.description: Whether publish_report may store reports and comments on the platform for this organisation (default true). Reports are client data beyond the Search Console and crawl data; an organisation may turn this off.

publish_confirm_kinds.description: Report kinds that need the person's explicit go before publish_report stores them: the tool answers needs_confirmation until re-called with confirm true. Intent, not a ban (default none). An organisation that only wants its SEO reports in Anchor by default sets ["custom"].

publish_confirm_without_property.description: When true, a publish_report call with no property needs the person's go the same way (default false)

tools.name: get_incidents
tools.description: Did something break on pages that earn traffic? Incidents = NEW or WORSENING findings in categories Google acts on (response codes, directives, canonicals) whose URLs carry at least the organisation's incident_click_threshold clicks/28d (steering, default 50). Each incident lists its top URLs with three views: what Google last reported (Page Indexing category), what our crawler saw (status, indexability, canonical), and a live URL Inspection verdict when auto_inspect_incidents is on and daily budget remains. Lead reports with this; fall back to get_audit_report for the full picture.

snapshot.description: Crawl snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to latest)

compare.description: Baseline snapshot (defaults to the comparable previous crawl; "none" disables)

threshold.description: Override the click threshold for this call

inspect.description: Override auto-inspect for this call (spends URL Inspection quota)

tools.name: inspect_url
tools.description: Inspect up to 10 URLs against the LIVE Google index via the URL Inspection API: verdict, coverage state, last crawl time, Google-selected canonical, robots state. Uses the property's own Search Console account. Spends real quota (Anchor budgets a few hundred per property per day; a result from the last 24 h is reused unless force=true) — inspect samples, not populations.

force.description: Re-inspect even if a result from the last 24 h exists

tools.name: archive_report
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) a report this organisation published, or restore one with restore true: it disappears from list_reports and the Reports page and takes no more comments, but every version and comment is kept and restoring brings them back. Use it for a report published by mistake (the wrong organisation's document, a test) or one nobody needs any more. Ask the person before archiving and tell them what will be hidden. Republishing an archived slug needs publish_report with restore true.

restore.description: true brings an archived report back

tools.name: list_reports
tools.description: The reports this organisation has published into Anchor: slug, title, kind, status (draft / in_review / final), current version, property, snapshot, open comment count, alternate formats and URL. Archived reports are left out unless include_archived is true. Filter by property, kind or status. Use it before publish_report to reuse a slug, and before an audit or monitor run to find the report whose comments to read.

tools.name: get_report_comments
tools.description: The review comments people left on a published report, threaded, each with its anchor (block_id and the quoted text it was written on), author and whether it is resolved. Defaults to open comments on the current version. The loop: read them before the next audit or monitor run, apply what you accept to the report, republish with publish_report (same slug), then resolve_comment each comment you applied; leave the rest open and say why in the republished text.

version.description: A specific version (default: the current one)

tools.name: resolve_comment
tools.description: Mark a report comment resolved after you applied it (or reopen it with resolved=false). Recorded with who resolved it. Only comments on reports in this organisation.

tools.name: preview_digest
tools.description: The digest this organisation's report recipients would receive now (subject, per-property numbers, top findings) — composed from the same data as the audit tools, never sent by this tool. Use it to show someone what the weekly email will say, or to check the numbers before a cadence change.

tools.name: report_issue
tools.description: Report a problem with the Anchor platform itself — wrong or inconsistent data, a tool that is missing or errored, something slow or confusing. Use it whenever the work was harder than it should have been; one call per distinct problem. The report is stored with your org and key and mirrored as a GitHub issue for the Tight Ship team. Not for SEO findings about a site (those belong in the audit).

category.description: What kind of problem. 'steering' = a steering improvement: you had to improvise beyond the organisation's steering, or the person asked for something it does not cover — put the field and the wording you propose in the description

title.description: One line, specific: "get_finding_urls returns 0 rows for a finding with 88 URLs"

description.description: What you expected, what happened, and what you were trying to do. Include the exact numbers or error text.

property.description: Domain the problem occurred on, if any

tool_name.description: The anchor-seo tool involved, if any

context.description: Anything useful to reproduce: the arguments you passed, the error text, counts you compared

tools.name: list_reported_issues
tools.description: Issues previously reported through report_issue (your org only in remote mode), newest first. Use to avoid duplicate reports or to see what is already known. Reads are immediately consistent, but call it AFTER report_issue has returned, not in the same parallel batch.

since.description: Only reports after this ISO timestamp or YYYY-MM-DD

category.description: Filter by category; 'steering' lists proposed steering improvements

tools.name: get_tracked_issues
tools.description: List tracked issues (expert-curated root causes) for a property: each associates GSC categories + SF issue types scoped by page types, with lifecycle status, computed URL population at the latest snapshot, and suggested_status. Resolved issues are hidden unless include_resolved.

tools.name: get_tracked_issue_report
tools.description: The full canonical payload for one tracked issue: scope, signals, computed population (union/gsc/sf/both counts, per-signal breakdown, sample URLs, 28d clicks), lifecycle with baseline + suggested_status (never auto-applied — confirm transitions with set_tracked_issue_status), evidence timeline, and machine-readable actions (pass actions.recrawl.params to recrawl_issues, etc.).

snapshot.description: Compute population at this snapshot YYYY-MM-DD (default latest complete crawl snapshot)

tools.name: get_validation_status
tools.description: Per-URL validation-submission counts by reason and status (submitted / validated / cleared) for a property — the rows record_validation and submit_validation write. Run reconcile_validations after a new snapshot to flip cleared URLs to validated; get_validation_candidates says which reasons are worth validating next.

tools.name: get_validation_candidates
tools.description: Which Page Indexing reasons are worth a Search Console "Validate fix" right now, per reason: how many of its sampled URLs the latest crawl shows in a state that contradicts the reason AND is live for Googlebot (live = 200 + indexable; migrated = 301 whose target is 200 + indexable; removed = 404/410; the two Duplicate reasons also accept canonicalised-elsewhere / noindex), the gate (ready / not_ready / n/a with gate_reason), sample URLs, the last recorded validation, and a recommended_action of validate for ready reasons only. The gate holds back redirects whose targets are not live, reasons the crawl cannot judge (robots.txt), Google-quality verdicts (Crawled/Discovered - currently not indexed, unless a migration moved them), and reasons with a validation already running. "Validate fix" is a Search Console UI button with no API: the person clicks it (Pages → the reason → Validate fix) with their go, one validation per reason at a time, results in days to weeks; then call record_validation.

snapshot.description: Crawl snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD (mapped to its source GSC date) or a GSC date; default latest GSC snapshot

tools.name: record_validation
tools.description: Record that a person started "Validate fix" in Search Console for one Page Indexing reason (there is no API, so this is how the platform learns about it). Writes the run (reason, date, Google's URL count, note) and seeds a per-URL row for every sampled URL of that reason at the snapshot, so reconcile_validations can mark them validated when a newer snapshot no longer lists them. Call it only after the person confirms they clicked; one validation per reason at a time. Not a platform action: nothing is sent to Google.

gsc_category.description: The reason exactly as Search Console names it (e.g. "Not found (404)")

submitted_on.description: Date the person clicked Validate fix, YYYY-MM-DD (default today)

url_count.description: The page count Search Console showed for the reason (default: the snapshot's chart total)

note.description: Context: what was fixed, which hosts, the ticket

snapshot.description: GSC or crawl snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD whose URL list backs the run (default: newest complete snapshot on or before submitted_on)

tools.name: submit_validation
tools.description: Per-URL variant of record_validation: mark specific URLs as submitted to Search Console for re-validation (action="submit"), or un-submit them (action="clear"). Use record_validation for the normal case (one "Validate fix" click covers a whole reason); use this when the person validated a subset or you need to clear rows. Not a platform action — it records what a person did in Search Console; nothing is sent to Google.

gsc_category.description: The GSC category being validated (e.g. "Not found (404)")

tools.name: reconcile_validations
tools.description: Refresh the validation read model: flip "submitted" per-URL records to "validated" where the URL no longer appears in its reason at the latest complete GSC snapshot newer than the submission (mig 102). Run it after every new snapshot (the monitor recipe does) and report validated / still_flagged. Idempotent; a partial snapshot missing the whole reason never validates anything. Not a platform action.

tools.name: get_data_dictionary
tools.description: The steering doc for raw data: sampling caps, paired snapshot dates, segment overlap, forward-fill, known import caveats. READ THIS before analyzing raw exports or crawl CSVs — every documented trap produces plausible-but-wrong conclusions.

tools.name: list_raw_exports
tools.description: Manifest of raw files for a property: GSC export ZIPs per (snapshot, segment, category) and complete SF crawl jobs with stored CSV results. Defaults to the two most recent GSC dates (one scrape session writes a chart-date/export-date pair). Start here before get_gsc_export / query_crawl_data.

snapshot.description: Limit to one snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: query_crawl_data
tools.description: Run one read-only SELECT (DuckDB SQL) over a Screaming Frog crawl's raw CSVs. Table names = CSV basenames (internal_html is the master URL table; issue CSVs exist only when the crawl found that issue — absent = zero). Results capped at 500 rows. Call with SQL referencing no known table to list available tables.

sql.description: A single SELECT/WITH statement. Tables are the crawl CSV basenames.

snapshot.description: SF crawl snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to the largest recent crawl)

tools.name: get_crawl_file_urls
tools.description: Manifest of a crawl's raw CSV files with short-lived presigned download URLs (15 min) for bulk client-side analysis. Falls back to a URL-less manifest when the deployment cannot sign (use query_crawl_data instead there).

snapshot.description: SF crawl snapshot date YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to the largest recent crawl)
